meta.title: Glossary | ProxMenux Documentation
meta.description: Definitions of the technical terms used throughout the ProxMenux documentation — Proxmox concepts (VM, LXC, qm, pct, pmxcfs), virtualization fundamentals (KVM, IOMMU, VFIO, OVMF), storage (ZFS, ARC, LVM, vzdump, PBS), network (bridge, VLAN, nftables) and ProxMenux-specific terminology.
meta.ogDescription: Quick reference for the technical terms used across the ProxMenux documentation.

header.title: Glossary
header.description: Definitions of the technical terms used throughout the ProxMenux documentation. Covers Proxmox concepts, virtualization fundamentals, storage, networking, Linux internals and ProxMenux-specific terminology.

callout.title: How to use this page
callout.bodyRich: Each entry has a category badge and a short definition. See also links jump to the doc page where the term is most relevant. Use the A–Z navigation below to scroll directly to a letter.

missingCallout.title: Missing a term?
missingCallout.leadRich: If a term in the docs is missing, open an issue or PR on GitHub. Glossary content lives in web/messages/en/docs/glossary.json, with matching locale catalogs.

entries.definitionRich: PCIe access-control features that help isolate device traffic. IOMMU grouping depends on hardware and topology. The ACS override kernel patch can split groups reported by Linux, but does not add hardware isolation; assigning those devices to separate VMs carries a security risk.

seeAlso.label: Add Controller or NVMe to VM

entries.definitionRich: ZFS read cache in host RAM, holding recently and frequently used data blocks. Its default limit depends on the Proxmox version and installation settings. ProxMenux Post-Install offers an option to cap it.
A Linux feature that exposes one part of the filesystem at another path. ProxMenux uses bind mounts to share host directories with LXC containers via pct set -mpN.
Combines multiple physical network interfaces into one logical interface — for redundancy (active-backup), throughput (LACP / 802.3ad) or both. Configured in /etc/network/interfaces.

A virtual layer-2 switch on the host. vmbr0 commonly connects guests to the physical network. Additional bridges (vmbr1, vmbr2...) can separate guest networks, depending on their physical links and configuration.

Distributed storage integrated with Proxmox for hyper-converged clusters. OSDs (Object Storage Daemons) underpin its object, block and file storage. Required Ceph versions depend on the Proxmox release and upgrade path; consult the corresponding upgrade guide.
Short for "container" — Proxmox terminology for an LXC instance. Has a numeric CTID that maps to /etc/pve/lxc/<CTID>.conf. See also LXC.

Modern format for APT repository sources, using .sources files with structured key/value blocks (Types, URIs, Suites, Components, Signed-By). Replaces the legacy single-line .list format. Standard from PVE 9 / Debian Trixie onward.

A separate graphics card, typically connected over PCIe, unlike an iGPU. It can be assigned to a VM with VFIO or accessed by multiple LXC containers through device nodes and the host driver, subject to hardware and application support.
ncurses-based tool for drawing menus, prompts and progress bars in a terminal. ProxMenux is built around dialog menus.
Framework for rebuilding registered out-of-tree kernel modules, such as NVIDIA or ZFS, when the kernel changes. Successful builds still require compatible module sources and matching kernel headers.

Intrusion prevention service that watches log files for repeated authentication failures and bans the offending IPs at the firewall layer. ProxMenux ships pre-configured jails for SSH, the Proxmox UI and the Monitor.
ASCII-art system info tool that runs on shell login (the "system summary banner"). Replaces the older neofetch; available as an opt-in option in ProxMenux Post-Install.

Boot loader used on GRUB-based Linux installations. Configuration is in /etc/default/grub and /boot/grub/; run update-grub after edits. Other Proxmox boot setups may use systemd-boot, so check the active boot loader before changing kernel parameters.

Graphics processor built into the CPU package (Intel UHD / Iris, AMD Radeon Vega in Ryzen APUs). Typically shared across multiple LXC containers via /dev/dri rather than passed through to a single VM.
The classic Debian network configuration system that reads /etc/network/interfaces. ifupdown2 is the rewritten version Proxmox uses by default — supports live reload via ifreload -a.

Initial RAM filesystem the kernel uses at boot before the real root filesystem is mounted. Contains drivers needed early (storage, encryption, RAID). Rebuilt with update-initramfs -u -k all after VFIO, IOMMU or storage driver changes.

Hardware feature (Intel VT-d / AMD-Vi) needed for PCIe passthrough to VMs. Enable it in firmware and ensure kernel support is active. Kernel arguments such as intel_iommu=on or amd_iommu=on may be needed, depending on platform and kernel defaults.

A set of devices that forms the smallest IOMMU isolation boundary. Devices within a group are not necessarily isolated from one another; review every member before VFIO assignment. Listed via find /sys/kernel/iommu_groups/ -type l | sort -V.
Network protocol that exposes block storage over IP — a remote disk appears as a local SCSI device. Registered as Proxmox storage via pvesm add iscsi.

seeAlso.label: Add iSCSI target as Proxmox storage

entries.definitionRich: Linux kernel module that turns the host into a hypervisor. Combined with QEMU for device emulation, it's the foundation Proxmox uses to run VMs.

Linux volume-management layer that groups physical storage into volume groups (VG) containing logical volumes (LV). LVM-based Proxmox installations commonly use LVM-thin for guest disks; other backends are available. Tools include pvs, vgs and lvs.

OS-level virtualization in which isolated userspace instances share the host kernel. Usually has less overhead than VMs, with a different isolation boundary. Proxmox manages LXC containers with the pct CLI.

Open-source security auditor (by CISOfy) that scans the host and prints a hardening score plus concrete remediation hints. ProxMenux installs the latest from upstream GitHub rather than the (older) Debian package.

Usually a 48-bit Ethernet interface identifier, assigned by hardware or software. ProxMenux Persistent Network Names matches MAC addresses to stable interface names (eno1, enp3s0) to keep names consistent after PCI re-enumeration.
Text displayed after SSH login, stored in /etc/motd. ProxMenux Post-Install can add a banner; the uninstaller restores the previous file when a backup exists.
Unix-native network file sharing protocol. Registered as Proxmox storage via pvesm add nfs; also usable as an LXC client / server via dedicated ProxMenux flows.

Linux firewall tooling. nftables is the modern framework; iptables can use legacy or nft-compatible backends. Classic pve-firewall uses iptables, while the alternative proxmox-firewall backend uses nftables.

Open-source NVIDIA graphics driver included with the Linux kernel. When installing the proprietary NVIDIA driver, prevent nouveau from binding the same GPU, usually by blacklisting it and rebuilding initramfs.

Proxmox package repository available without an enterprise subscription. Packages receive less validation than in the enterprise repository, which Proxmox recommends for production. ProxMenux Post-Install offers repository configuration.

DMTF formats for packaging portable VMs. OVA packages the files in a single TAR archive; OVF describes the VM in XML with accompanying disk files, commonly VMDK. Import support depends on the target hypervisor and configuration.

UEFI firmware for VMs, selected with qm set <vmid> -bios ovmf. Used for UEFI guests, including Windows 11 and Secure Boot configurations. An efidisk0 stores persistent EFI variables; many other guests can still use legacy BIOS.

Separate Proxmox backup product providing incremental transfers, deduplication and optional client-side encryption for VM and CT backups. It can be used as a vzdump destination; a separate backup server is preferable to keeping backups on the protected host.
CLI tool for managing LXC containers in Proxmox: pct list / start / stop / shutdown / config / enter / exec / push / pull / destroy.
FUSE-based virtual filesystem mounted at /etc/pve/. Replicates configuration changes across all cluster nodes in real time. Editing a file under /etc/pve/ propagates automatically.
CLI for managing the local catalog of CT templates. pveam update refreshes the index; pveam available lists templates; pveam download <storage> <template> downloads one.

The HTTPS service that serves the Proxmox web UI on port 8006 and the web terminal. Restarted automatically during major upgrades — which is why ProxMenux refuses to run the PVE 8 → 9 upgrade from the web terminal.
CLI tool for managing Proxmox storage. pvesm status shows all configured storages; pvesm add <type> registers new ones (NFS, Samba, iSCSI, dir, ZFS, LVM, …).

LXC container whose root user maps to host UID 0, while namespaces and other restrictions still apply. Less isolated than an unprivileged container. GPU, USB and Samba access do not universally require this mode; permissions and UID mappings matter.
Optional web dashboard installed alongside ProxMenux. Serves real-time host stats (CPU / RAM / disk / network), VM and LXC overview, login + 2FA, on TCP port 8008.
VM disk image format commonly used on directory storage. Supports allocation on demand, snapshots and copy-on-write. Convert an image with qemu-img convert -O qcow2 ....
CLI tool for managing VMs in Proxmox: qm list / start / stop / shutdown / config / set / destroy / importdisk / migrate. Sister command of pct for containers.

Modern QEMU machine type emulating an Intel Q35 chipset with PCIe support. Recommended over the older i440FX for VMs that need PCIe passthrough or modern guest OS support. Set with qm set <vmid> -machine q35.
Generic, open-source machine emulator and virtualizer. Combined with KVM in Proxmox to run VMs at near-native speed.

Command-line tool supporting many cloud storage providers, including Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Mega and S3. The cloud-backup guide uses it to mount remote storage as a directory for vzdump archives.
Microsoft's file-sharing protocol family. SMB is the protocol; Samba is the open-source Linux implementation; CIFS is an older SMB dialect. Registered as Proxmox storage via pvesm add cifs.
Open-source legacy BIOS implementation used by QEMU. Default firmware for new VMs unless you switch to OVMF. Suitable for older OSes and simple Linux installs that don't need UEFI.
Built-in disk diagnostics that report drive health, error counts and self-test results. smartctl (from smartmontools) is the CLI; for NVMe drives, the nvme-cli package adds NVMe-specific commands.
Modern init system used by Debian / Proxmox. systemctl manages services (start / stop / enable / status). journalctl reads the binary log written by systemd-journald.

Tool for reading and changing kernel parameters. Persistent settings are commonly placed in /etc/sysctl.d/*.conf; support for /etc/sysctl.conf depends on the loader. ProxMenux Post-Install offers a sysctl tuning profile.
Codename for Debian 13, the OS base for Proxmox VE 9. Predecessor: bookworm (Debian 12 / PVE 8).

Linux device manager. Reacts to hardware events and creates / removes entries under /dev. Custom rules in /etc/udev/rules.d/ persistently map MAC addresses to interface names, set up NVIDIA device nodes on driver load, etc.

With the default mapping in unprivileged LXC containers, host UIDs and GIDs are shifted by +100000: container UID 0 maps to host UID 100000, and 1000 to 101000. Custom mappings can differ; file ownership on bind mounts must match the chosen mapping.

LXC container whose root maps to an unprivileged host UID, normally 100000. This reduces host privileges while sharing its kernel. Hardware access can still be configured with suitable device permissions and mappings; privileged mode is not universally required.

Linux kernel framework for safe userspace device drivers — used to bind PCIe devices to VMs for direct passthrough. Enabled by loading the vfio, vfio_iommu_type1 and vfio_pci kernel modules, configured via /etc/modprobe.d/vfio.conf.

Family of paravirtualized device drivers (network, storage, balloon, GPU) that run faster than emulated legacy hardware (e.g. e1000 NICs, IDE disks). The guest needs the matching VirtIO driver — kernel-native on Linux, separate ISO install on Windows.
802.1Q tags that segment one physical network into multiple logical networks. Configured per-bridge or per-NIC in /etc/network/interfaces.

Virtual machine managed by Proxmox with QEMU/KVM, running its own guest kernel. Its numeric VMID maps to /etc/pve/qemu-server/<VMID>.conf. Usually has more overhead than LXC, with a separate kernel isolation boundary.

Proxmox backup tool for VMs and CTs. File archives are not incremental; PBS targets support incremental transfers. Jobs can configure backup mode (snapshot / suspend / stop), compression (such as zstd, gzip or lzo), retention and notifications.

Combined filesystem and volume manager with snapshots, send/receive replication, checksums and compression. It can repair corrupted data when a valid redundant copy is available. Read caching uses RAM through ARC, whose size can be limited.
